description: Hand-authored synthetic publication records and query-to-record relevance judgments. Not institutional, scientific, or live-source validation.

candidates.title: Field validation of image-based maize disease detection
candidates.abstract: This synthetic study trains image classifiers to identify fungal disease in maize leaves collected from smallholder farms. Field validation compares model alerts with laboratory diagnosis and agronomist assessment across multiple growing seasons.

candidates.title: Low-cost camera screening of crop infections in small farms
candidates.abstract: Farmers photograph damaged foliage with basic mobile devices, and plant-health workers confirm suspected infections during field visits. The study measures whether image triage can identify outbreaks early enough to guide crop protection.

candidates.title: Community reporting of crop disease outbreaks
candidates.abstract: Agricultural extension workers combine farmer reports and periodic field observations to map plant disease incidence. The work studies surveillance coverage and response time but does not classify photographs or train an image model.

candidates.title: Maize leaf image analysis for nutrient deficiency rather than infection
candidates.abstract: A computer-vision system classifies nitrogen and potassium stress in maize leaves from field photographs. Pathogen detection is explicitly outside scope, although the imagery, crop, and image-classification terminology overlap with disease-screening research.

candidates.title: Remote-sensing estimates of seasonal crop yield
candidates.abstract: Satellite vegetation indices and rainfall histories are combined to estimate regional harvest volumes. The analysis supports food-supply planning and contains no plant-disease diagnosis or leaf-image classification.

candidates.title: Image-based maize disease detection validated in farm fields
candidates.abstract: This duplicate synthetic metadata record describes the same work as PUB-AGR-01 under a reordered title and a DOI URL.

candidates.title: Clinical prediction and referral for high-risk pregnancies
candidates.abstract: This synthetic clinical study develops a risk model to identify pregnant patients needing escalation and evaluates referrals from community providers to facilities. Outcomes include timely care, severe complications, and referral completion.

candidates.title: Referral and clinical prediction for high-risk pregnancy
candidates.abstract: This duplicate synthetic metadata record describes the same work as PUB-MAT-01 under a reordered title and a DOI URL.

candidates.title: Routing expectant mothers with warning signs to emergency obstetric care
candidates.abstract: Community health workers use a structured triage pathway to connect women showing danger signs with facilities able to provide urgent obstetric services. The evaluation follows referral decisions and maternal outcomes.

candidates.title: Mobile maternal-health education and antenatal appointment reminders
candidates.abstract: Text messages provide pregnancy education and reminders to attend routine antenatal visits. The programme measures knowledge and appointment attendance but does not estimate individual clinical risk or direct high-risk referrals.

candidates.title: Referral directory for maternity services
Detecting contamination events from drinking-water sensor streams
candidates.abstract: This synthetic engineering study analyses continuous chemical and microbial measurements from drinking-water probes. It identifies anomalous contamination signatures and validates alerts against laboratory samples collected at distribution points.

candidates.title: Early warning for unsafe water using automated probe readings
candidates.abstract: A monitoring network flags unusual combinations of turbidity, conductivity, and microbial indicators before routine sampling would detect a problem. The study evaluates warning accuracy and response time for drinking-water contamination.

candidates.title: Community field-kit testing of rural water sources
candidates.abstract: Local teams test wells and springs with portable kits and report results to district water officers. The project examines sampling access and community response but does not use continuous sensor streams or anomaly detection.

candidates.title: Sensor-based scheduling of irrigation from reservoirs
candidates.abstract: Water-level probes and weather forecasts guide irrigation releases to reduce crop water shortages. The work shares water monitoring and sensor terminology but studies agricultural allocation, not contamination or drinking-water safety.

candidates.title: Forecasting photovoltaic output from weather observations
candidates.abstract: This synthetic energy study predicts solar-farm generation from irradiance, cloud cover, temperature, and wind measurements. Time-series forecasts are evaluated against observed output to support grid dispatch and storage planning.

candidates.title: Estimating sunlight-driven electricity production under changing clouds
candidates.abstract: A statistical model anticipates the power delivered by solar panels as atmospheric conditions change. It combines sky imagery and meteorological observations and evaluates short-term generation forecasts at distributed photovoltaic sites.

candidates.title: Solar mini-grid feasibility and household energy access
candidates.abstract: Geographic coverage, household demand, and installation cost are assessed to select locations for rural solar mini-grids. The research concerns infrastructure planning rather than forecasting photovoltaic output from weather data.

candidates.title: Weather-driven forecasts of electricity demand
candidates.abstract: Temperature and rainfall records are used to predict hourly electricity consumption by households. The forecasting method and meteorological inputs overlap lexically, but the target is demand rather than solar generation.

candidates.title: Improving early-grade reading comprehension through phonics instruction
candidates.abstract: This synthetic education study tests structured phonics lessons and guided reading in primary classrooms. Reading fluency and comprehension are measured before and after instruction across schools serving multilingual learners.

candidates.title: Helping young pupils decode unfamiliar words and understand short texts
candidates.abstract: Teachers use sound-letter activities and supported reading passages to strengthen literacy in the first years of school. The study measures decoding, oral fluency, and understanding among children learning in more than one language.

candidates.title: Teacher attendance and classroom resource availability
candidates.abstract: School visits document staff presence, textbook access, and lesson time in rural primary education. The study describes learning conditions but does not evaluate reading instruction or literacy outcomes.

candidates.title: Restoring native forest corridors to support pollinator diversity
candidates.abstract: This synthetic ecology study restores connected native vegetation and measures wild pollinator richness across fragmented landscapes. Repeated field surveys assess whether habitat corridors improve species persistence and movement between reserves.

candidates.title: Reconnecting fragmented habitats for wild-pollinator recovery
candidates.abstract: Researchers compare insect communities before and after planting native strips between isolated forest patches. The work tests whether landscape connectivity supports pollination services and the survival of locally observed species.

candidates.title: Farmer knowledge and conservation attitudes near forest reserves
candidates.abstract: Interviews examine local views about wildlife protection, reserve access, and conservation incentives. The study concerns community perspectives but does not restore habitat or measure pollinator diversity.

candidates.title: Tree planting for carbon storage in degraded landscapes
candidates.abstract: Native and introduced tree species are compared for biomass accumulation and carbon storage. The study uses restoration terminology but does not assess ecological corridors, pollinators, or biodiversity outcomes.
